full_judgment:
This Rule arises out of a judgment of reversal in a proceeding under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. 

 5. In 29 D LR at page 229 it has been stated in clear terms that if the re-conveyance takes place before the starting of the proceeding for pre-emption the right to pre-emption does not exist. In unreported decision in the case of Bandar Ali Halder Va. Kalu Halder and others Mr. Justice Ruhul Islam also found that if the re-conveyance takes place before the starting of the proceeding for pre-emption, the right to pre-emption ceases to exist. This view has also got support in a later decision report in I Bangladesh Case Report (1981) in the case of Mohan Ali Mandai Vs. Shahajuddin Mia Page 27, In this decision it has been held that when a land sought to be pre-empted has already gone back to its original owner by way of re-sale before an application for pre-emption is filed, then the whole matter ends there and no right of pre-emption subsists.
